newsitem.title: USA: Flat U.S. April IP seen having scant sway with Fed.
newsitem.headline: Flat U.S. April IP seen having scant sway with Fed.

text.p: Auto industry work stoppages kept the lid on U.S. industrial production in April, but economists say that phenomenon is temporary and that April's flat production will not be an influential factor in the Federal Reserve's deliberations on monetary policy next week.

"April was flat due to the auto strikes so that production will bounce back," said Charles Lieberman, chief economist at Chase Securities Inc. "(Excluding) autos, industrial production was up 0.3 percent (in April)."

With a 0.6 percent production rise in March, revised down from the 0.9 percent increase first reported, the numbers are "probably consistent with a picture of moderate ongoing gains in industrial activity," Lieberman said.
Analysts said the production data would be unlikely to sway the thinking of Fed policy makers when they meet on May 20 to mull another interest-rate hike.
"The data ... (indicate) that there is still very good momentum out there," said Astrid Adolfson, vice president at MCM Moneywatch Inc. "The (Fed) will look through this."
